resources.string: Shows the current date and time for cities you choose from around the world.
Tap to add or show cities

Pattern letters follow java.time.format.DateTimeFormatter: yyyy=year, MM=month, dd=day, EEE=weekday, HH=24h hour, hh=12h hour, mm=minute. For am/pm: lowercase \'a\' forces lowercase (am/pm), uppercase \'A\' forces uppercase (AM/PM).
No cities added yet. Tap \"Add city\" to get started.
Battery time left bar (bottom, full = 24 h)

Green above 60%, yellow 40–60%, red below 40%. Time left is estimated from how fast the battery drains while unplugged, so it fills in after the level drops a couple of percent. With no cities shown and only the level bar on, the whole widget becomes one large battery bar (brighter, with ⚡, while charging).

While charging the widget shows battery level, speed and current instead of the clocks. Pings every 2 min (5x), then every 5 min (5x), then every 10 min. When the charger is pulled, a 5 s alarm repeats every 5 min until you tap Stop. At 100% the widget shows the clocks again; after one final ping (or “Fully charged”), pings, speech and the unplug alarm stay quiet until the next charge. Tap the bell on the charging widget to mute charging sounds for the current charge only. Set per widget: sounds play once for the phone if any widget has them on, and only widgets with alerts on show the unplug alarm. Keeps a silent "Watching charger" notification.

While charging, says “Charged to 30 percent” each time the battery reaches the next step. A big jump is announced once, at the actual level (e.g. 9% to 22% says 22). Uses the notification volume and the phone’s text-to-speech voice.

resources.string: Changes are saved as you make them. Undo restores the settings you had when you opened this screen.

All World Time is published by LanDen Labs. It has no account, shows no ads and does not sell or share data.

City search is the only network use. When you type in Add city, the city name you type (the part before any comma) is sent to the free Open-Meteo geocoding service (open-meteo.com) to find matching cities and their time zones. Like any web request, Open-Meteo sees your IP address. Nothing else is sent: no location, settings, battery data or identifiers. The app contains no analytics, crash reporting or advertising code, and we never receive any of your data.

Stored only on your phone: the cities, colors, sizes and formats you choose for each widget; recent battery readings used to estimate the time left; and whether charging alerts are on. Android backup, if you turn it on, may back these settings up to your Google account.

Permissions: Internet (city search only), notifications (the unplug alarm and the “Watching charger” notice), a foreground service (to notice the charger being connected or unplugged), exact alarms (to play pings and the alarm on time), full-screen alarm, wake lock (while a sound plays) and run at startup. The app does not use location, camera, microphone, contacts, photos or storage.

Deleting data: removing a widget deletes its settings. Uninstalling the app or clearing its storage deletes everything.

Questions: landenlabs.app@gmail.com
